legend: Baba Yaga and her hut on chicken legs (Russia / Slavic folktale)
lines: Deep in the Russian forest stands a hut that walks on chicken legs.
It belongs to Baba Yaga, the witch of Slavic folktales.
She flies through the night in a giant mortar, sweeping away her tracks with a broom.
One evening, a lost traveler finds a fence lit by glowing skulls.
The hut spins around, and the door creaks open.
Baba Yaga leans out and sniffs the air. I smell a visitor!
She sets hard tasks for everyone who enters. Do them well, and you may go free.
Be rude, and the legends say you will never be seen again.
But the kind and the brave are said to leave with a gift.
Would you dare knock on her door?
title: The Witch With a Hut That Walks on Chicken Legs #shorts
description:
Deep in the Russian forest lives Baba Yaga, a witch whose hut walks on chicken legs. An old Slavic folktale about tests, warnings and gifts.
